exposure: Anorectal manometry (ARM) parameters (rectoanal gradient, rectal defecation pressure, anal squeeze pressure, anal resting pressure, rectal sensory function)
outcome: Transperineal ultrasound (TPUS) findings (anorectal angle during strain, rectocele, internal rectal intussusception, internal rectal prolapse, various pelvic floor anatomical abnormalities)
cohort: Female patients (n=296, with n=209 undergoing both tests) diagnosed with obstructive defecation syndrome (ODS).
finding: Circumscribed yet specific anatomic-functional correlations exist between select ARM and TPUS parameters in patients with ODS, with reduced anorectal pressure gradient being the strongest ARM predictor of an abnormal anorectal angle during defecation.
cross-section timing: At the time of evaluation for obstructive defecation syndrome.
